title: Rust, hands on
intro: Fourteen short chapters that take you from your first println to structs, ownership, and real Cargo projects. Every example in this book is compiled by the Rust compiler installed on this machine — when you press Run, nothing is simulated.

modules.title: Start the engine
modules.blurb: A program that runs, and bindings that hold values.

modules.title: Types and shapes
modules.blurb: Numbers, functions, and the control flow that drives them.

modules.title: Ownership
modules.blurb: The three rules that make Rust Rust. Read this twice.

modules.title: Types you build
modules.blurb: Structs group data. Enums choose between shapes.

modules.title: Collections and iteration
modules.blurb: Vectors, strings, maps, and chaining transformations.

modules.title: When things fail
modules.blurb: Panics, Results, and the question mark operator.

modules.title: Sharing behavior
modules.blurb: Traits and generics: one function, many types.

modules.title: Real projects
modules.blurb: Modules, Cargo layout, tests, and where to go next.

afterword.title: Keep going
afterword.body: You now have the vocabulary the rest of the Rust bookshelves assume. The Book is the long-form reference for everything here; Rust by Example is the same ideas as runnable programs; the Nomicon is for the day you write unsafe code; the API documentation is where you will spend most of your actual working life.
